chapter_note: A compact three-fold cosmological teaching about modes of absolute stability ('rocks') established in the cosmic structure. The oldest teaching layer is dominant: a thesis paragraph, three enumerated items, and a summary recapitulation. The only significant editorial intrusion is in ¶5, where the third rock's cosmic placement has been replaced with 'the holy church' — an institutional substitution visible by comparison with ¶3's cosmic location ('this zone') and ¶6's summary ('three great places of these selfsame worlds'). The chapter otherwise preserves clean substrate with systematic emanation and placement patterns.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic dialogue frame: 'Once again he speaks to his disciples.' No cosmological content whatsoever.

paragraphs.core_text: Three great rocks, which exist, were appointed by the greatness. They were set in these outer worlds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Thesis statement introducing the teaching. 'The greatness' is cosmic agency; 'these outer worlds' is cosmic geography. Both sides of the mapping stay within the cosmic system. Sets up a three-fold enumeration.

paragraphs.core_text: So, the first rock is the [Pillar] of Glory, the Perfect Man, which was summoned [by the] glorious Ambassador. He set it in this zone; [ ... he] brought forth its base (?) from the earth to heaven. It bore up under the [en]tire uni[verse], and became first of all the weight-carriers in [it]s powers. In its firmness it has been set upright, and has made fast every [t]hing above and below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration item. Pillar of Glory / Perfect Man — cosmic entity. Summoned by the Ambassador — cosmic emanation. 'This zone' — cosmic location. Function described entirely within the cosmic architecture (bearing up the universe, weight-carriers, firmness above and below). Classic substrate pattern: entity → summoner → location → function. Lacunae preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] second great and glorious rock is the new earth of light, which was set upon the earth of Darkness. It has squashed the fastenings of the five storehouses of death. It has established firmness, with great firmness, over and beyond the earth of Darkness. It has flattened, crushed and fixed the root of death.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration item. 'New earth of light' set upon 'earth of Darkness' — cosmic geography. 'Five storehouses of death' — systematic five-fold cosmological nomenclature (the five dark realms). 'Root of death' — cosmic entity. All mappings cosmos→cosmos. The substrate vocabulary score (16.36) is the highest in the chapter.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] third rock is the great thought, which was summoned from Jesus, the glorious one. It has stood firm, with a true fixity, for ever.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed: 'He set it in the holy church. The church gathered in upon it, and has lived in [it].' — Institutional layer. The expected cosmic location (cf. 'this zone' in ¶3, 'upon the earth of darkness' in ¶4) has been replaced with 'the holy church.' The summary paragraph ¶6 confirms the original by saying all three were in 'three great places of these selfsame worlds' — cosmic geography incompatible with a terrestrial institution. The editor extended the cosmic placement pattern to the Manichaean community.
paragraphs.temporal_note: 'Summoned from Jesus, the glorious one' parallels 'summoned by the glorious Ambassador' in ¶3 — this is the cosmic emanation pattern (Jesus the Splendor as cosmic figure, not historical Jesus). The institutional vocabulary score (16.28) fires only here. 'It has stood firm, with a true fixity, for ever' describes the rock's quality (paralleling firmness language in ¶3 and ¶4) and is retained as substrate. The institutional insertion ('holy church') breaks the cosmic-location pattern established by the first two rocks.

paragraphs.core_text: [These] are the three great rocks, they that have come forth in great confidence, in three great and honoured places. They were appointed and distributed in three great places of these [self]same worlds. They were made fast according to the will of the greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary recapitulation closing the enumeration. 'Three great places of these selfsame worlds' — cosmic geography that implicitly confirms all three rocks belong to the cosmic architecture. 'The will of the greatness' — cosmic agency. Both sides within the system. This summary actually provides evidence that the original third rock had a cosmic location, not an institutional one.
